input: A client has not booked in 5 months. Draft a short, warm win-back text that fits within the booking history below.
context: Client Dana booked a 60 minute deep tissue massage on 2025 01 12 and a 60 minute session on 2025 02 09. No bookings since. Average ticket 95 dollars. Preferred Saturday mornings.
expected: Hi Dana, it has been a little while since your last deep tissue session in February. Saturday mornings are open again if you would like to come back in. Reply yes and we will hold a 60 minute slot for you.

input: Write a win-back message for a lapsed client without inventing any offer the owner did not approve.
context: Client Marcus last visited 2025 03 03. No discount has been approved by the owner. Owner policy is to never promise a price cut in automated messages.
expected: Hi Marcus, we have missed you since March. If you would like to come back in, reply here and we will find a time that works for your schedule.

input: A 2pm slot just opened from a cancellation. Draft an outreach to the most likely client to fill it today.
context: Today is Tuesday. A 2pm 30 minute slot opened at 1140am from a cancellation. Client Priya has asked twice this month for a Tuesday afternoon time and is on the short notice list.
expected: Hi Priya, a Tuesday 2pm 30 minute slot just opened today. You mentioned wanting a Tuesday afternoon, so I am offering it to you first. Reply yes to claim it.

input: Draft a review request for a client who left happy yesterday.
context: Client Tom completed a haircut and beard trim yesterday and told the barber he was very happy. The shop collects reviews on Google. The review link is https://g.page/r/example-shop.
expected: Hi Tom, glad you were happy with the cut and beard trim yesterday. If you have a minute, a quick Google review really helps the shop: https://g.page/r/example-shop

input: A client asks why their card was charged 95 dollars. Answer using only the booking record.
context: Client Renee was charged 95 dollars on 2025 04 18 for a 60 minute deep tissue massage. The posted rate for that service is 95 dollars. No tip was added by the shop.
expected: Your card was charged 95 dollars on April 18 for the 60 minute deep tissue massage, which is the posted rate for that service. No tip was added by us.

input: A client asks for Friday at 3pm. Confirm or offer the nearest open time using the calendar below.
context: Friday 3pm is already booked for another client. The nearest open times on Friday are 2pm and 415pm, both 60 minute slots.
expected: Friday at 3pm is already booked, but I can offer you Friday at 2pm or 415pm, both 60 minute slots. Which one works for you?

input: A client missed their appointment this morning. Write a neutral, non-accusatory follow up that invites a rebook.
context: Client Alex missed a 9am appointment this morning. Shop policy charges no fee for a first missed appointment. The goal is to rebook, not to scold.
expected: Hi Alex, we had you down for 9am this morning and missed you. No worries and no fee this time. Want me to find you a new time this week?

input: Remind a member their plan renews soon, using only the plan details given.
context: Client Sofia is on the monthly wellness plan at 79 dollars per month. The plan renews on the 1st of each month and includes two 60 minute sessions. Next renewal is May 1.
expected: Hi Sofia, your monthly wellness plan at 79 dollars renews on May 1 and includes two 60 minute sessions. Let me know if you would like to schedule them.

input: A client asks about a refund. State the actual policy from the context without softening or inventing exceptions.
context: Shop refund policy: refunds are available within 7 days of purchase for unused service packages only. Used sessions are not refundable. There are no other exceptions.
expected: Refunds are available within 7 days of purchase for unused service packages only. Sessions you have already used are not refundable, and there are no other exceptions.

input: A customer got an estimate 3 weeks ago and never approved the work. Draft a follow up that quotes the exact estimate.
context: Customer Jordan received a brake pad and rotor estimate of 420 dollars on 2025 04 02 at the auto shop. The estimate is still valid. Parts are in stock.
expected: Hi Jordan, following up on your brake pad and rotor estimate of 420 dollars from April 2. The estimate is still good and the parts are in stock. Want to get on the schedule?

input: Confirm a new consultation booking and restate the time so there is no confusion.
context: Client Bianca booked a free 20 minute intro consultation for Wednesday at 1030am. The consultation is by phone. Shop will call her.
expected: Hi Bianca, you are confirmed for a free 20 minute intro consultation on Wednesday at 1030am. It is by phone and we will call you. See you then.

input: Write a winback text for Dana, who hasn't booked in 6 months.
context: Client: Dana. Last visit: 6 months ago. Service: deep tissue massage $95. Policy: winback offers may include up to 10% off. Use code COMEBACK10. No pressure tone required.
expected: Hi Dana, we noticed it's been a while and we'd love to welcome you back. If you'd like another deep tissue massage, code COMEBACK10 takes 10% off — no pressure, just an open invitation.

input: Winback message for Maya, who asked not to be marketed to last year.
context: Client: Maya. Note: client asked to be removed from marketing outreach in 2025. Policy: respect opt-outs; do not send promotions. A single re-permission check is allowed.
expected: Hi Maya, checking in once: would you like to stay off our marketing list, or are you open to occasional updates? No pressure either way — just reply STOP to stay opted out and we won't ask again.

input: Announce our new hot stone add-on to a lapsed client, Sam.
context: Client: Sam. Lapsed 4 months. New service: hot stone add-on $25, launched March 2026. No pressure tone required. Approved winback copy must name the service and price exactly.
expected: Hi Sam, hope you're well — we're adding a hot stone add-on ($25) to our menu this spring. If you'd like to try it on your next visit, just ask when you book. No pressure, it's here whenever you want it.

input: The client wants to move Thursday's 2pm facial to Friday.
context: Policy: reschedules are free with 24 hours notice; no fees apply. Current booking: Thursday 2pm. Friday availability: 10am, 1pm, 3pm. Service: signature facial $85, 60 minutes.
expected: Of course — we can move your signature facial ($85) off Thursday 2pm at no charge since you're giving more than 24 hours notice. We have Friday at 10am, 1pm, or 3pm. Which works best for you?

input: We're fully booked Saturday. Put the client on the waitlist.
context: Policy: Saturday books out by Wednesday. Waitlist rule: confirmations go out by 6pm the day before. Deposit: $20 to hold a waitlist spot, refundable if no slot opens.
expected: Saturday is fully booked, but I can put you on the waitlist. We confirm open slots by 6pm Friday. A $20 deposit holds your spot, refunded automatically at 6pm Friday if the waitlist clears without a slot for you.

input: The client booked a 60-minute massage but now wants 90 minutes.
context: Pricing: 60 minutes $95, 90 minutes $140. Policy: upgrades are allowed if the therapist's schedule permits. Next slot after the booking: 4pm.
expected: We can extend your booking from 60 to 90 minutes — the price moves from $95 to $140, and it works as long as the therapist has room before the 4pm slot. Want me to check with them?

input: The client lost the receipt for last Tuesday's visit.
context: Visit: Tuesday, signature facial $85 plus $12 tip, total $97. Policy: receipts can be re-sent by email within 90 days of the visit.
expected: I can re-send your receipt by email — last Tuesday was the signature facial at $85 plus a $12 tip, for a total of $97. Just confirm the email address you'd like it sent to.

input: Explain how tipping works here.
context: Tipping guide: 15% to 20% is customary. On a $95 service, 20% is $19. Tips go directly to the therapist. Cash and card tips accepted.
expected: Tipping is entirely your call — 15% to 20% is customary, so on a $95 service a 20% tip works out to $19. Every bit of the tip goes directly to your therapist, and we accept both cash and card.

input: Do I have to pay anything to book?
context: Booking policy: a $30 deposit is required for appointments over $100. Deposits apply to the final bill. Deposits are refundable with 24-hour cancellation notice.
expected: Only a deposit for larger bookings — appointments over $100 need a $30 deposit, which comes off your final bill. Cancel with 24 hours notice and the deposit is fully refundable.

input: Remind Alex his membership renews next week.
context: Member: Alex. Plan: monthly membership $79, renews on the 1st. Perk: members get 10% off add-ons. Policy: reminders go out 7 days before renewal.
expected: Hi Alex, a friendly heads-up — your $79 monthly membership renews on the 1st. Remember you get 10% off add-ons as a member, and you can pause or cancel any time before renewal day.

input: Can I pause my membership for the summer?
context: Policy: memberships can be paused for 1 to 3 months per year. Billing resumes automatically when the pause ends. Pauses take effect on the 1st of the next month.
expected: Yes — you can pause for 1 to 3 months per year. The pause starts on the 1st of next month and billing picks back up automatically when it ends. How many months would you like to pause?

input: Cancel my membership effective immediately.
context: Policy: cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing cycle. No cancellation fee. The member keeps perks until the cycle ends.
expected: Done — your membership will stay active until the end of the current billing cycle, so you keep your perks until then. There's no cancellation fee, and you're welcome back any time.

input: The client wants a refund — the facial was fine but the massage was rushed.
context: Policy: partial refunds are allowed when part of a service was unsatisfactory. Combo booked: facial $85 + 30-min massage $55 = $140 total. Manager approval needed for refunds over $50.
expected: I'm sorry the massage felt rushed — let's make it right. The 30-minute massage portion was $55, and since that's over our $50 approval threshold I'll get a manager to sign off on refunding that part. The facial portion stays as booked.

input: Refund the no-show fee.
context: Policy: no-show fees are $25 and are non-refundable. Exception: documented emergencies may be reviewed by a manager.
expected: Our no-show fee is $25 and it's non-refundable under our policy. If this was a documented emergency, I can have a manager review it — otherwise the fee stands as charged.

input: Ask Dana for a review — she didn't respond to the first request.
context: Client: Dana. Last visit: signature facial $85. Policy: a maximum of two review requests per visit; do not send a third request. Requests must include an opt-out.
expected: Hi Dana, one last quick note about your visit — if you have a moment, we'd love a review of your signature facial. If you'd rather not hear about this again, just reply STOP and we'll take you off the list.

input: Reply to this 5-star review: 'Best facial of my life!'
context: Business: Glow Studio. Review: 5 stars, mentions facial. Policy: thank reviewers by name when given, invite them back, never offer incentives for reviews.
expected: Thank you so much for the 5 stars! We're thrilled the facial was a highlight — we'd love to welcome you back to Glow Studio whenever you're ready.

input: Follow up with a client who no-showed yesterday.
context: Client: Jordan. Missed appointment: Tuesday 3pm, deep tissue $95. Policy: first no-show gets a warning, second incurs a $25 fee.
expected: Hi Jordan, we missed you yesterday for your Tuesday 3pm deep tissue appointment. This counts as a first no-show, which comes with a warning rather than a charge — a second missed visit carries a $25 fee. Want to rebook?

input: The client no-showed again. Apply the fee.
context: Client: Jordan. This is the second no-show. Policy: second no-show incurs a $25 fee, charged to the card on file. Card on file: yes.
expected: Hi Jordan, since this is a second missed visit, the $25 no-show fee applies and will be charged to the card on file. We'd still love to see you — reply if you'd like to rebook.

input: Fill a last-minute cancellation for tomorrow morning.
context: Opening: tomorrow 9am, 60-min deep tissue $95. Waitlist: Priya (prefers mornings), Sam (any time). Policy: offer the slot to waitlist clients in order, first reply wins.
expected: Hi Priya, a spot just opened tomorrow at 9am for a 60-minute deep tissue session ($95). You're first on the waitlist since you prefer mornings — want it? First to reply gets the slot.

input: Two cancellations came in for Friday. Notify the waitlist.
context: Openings: Friday 11am and Friday 2pm, signature facial $85 each. Waitlist order: Maya, then Leo. Policy: offer both slots, first reply picks.
expected: Hi Maya, two Friday openings just came up for the signature facial ($85): 11am and 2pm. As first on the waitlist you get first pick — reply with the time you want and it's yours.

input: Confirm the consultation booking for Thursday.
context: Booking: Thursday 1pm, 30-min consultation, free of charge. Client: Robin. Policy: consultations are free and carry no deposit. Reminder text goes out 24 hours ahead.
expected: Hi Robin, confirming your free 30-minute consultation this Thursday at 1pm. There's no deposit and no charge — we'll also send a reminder text 24 hours ahead. See you Thursday!

input: What should the client do before the consultation?
context: Consultation prep: arrive 10 minutes early. Bring a list of current skincare products. Avoid heavy makeup. The consultation lasts 30 minutes and is free.
expected: Please arrive about 10 minutes early, bring a list of the skincare products you currently use, and skip heavy makeup that day. The consultation runs 30 minutes and is free.

input: Break down the brake repair estimate for the customer.
context: Estimate: front brake pads $120, labor 2 hours at $95/hr = $190, shop supplies $15. Total: $325. Warranty: 12 months on parts.
expected: Here's your brake estimate: front brake pads $120, labor $190 (2 hours at $95/hr), and $15 in shop supplies — $325 total. The pads carry a 12-month parts warranty.

input: The customer asks if the alternator replacement is still under warranty.
context: Repair: alternator replacement on 2025-06-01, $480. Warranty: 12 months parts, 6 months labor. Today: 2026-09-17. Policy: warranty claims need the original invoice.
expected: The alternator was replaced on 2025-06-01 with a 12-month parts warranty, so the parts coverage has ended as of today. If you have the original invoice I can still check whether anything else applies.

input: What are your hours and is there parking?
context: Hours: Tue-Sat 9am-7pm, closed Sun-Mon. Parking: free lot behind the building, entrance on Elm St.
expected: We're open Tuesday through Saturday, 9am to 7pm, and closed Sunday and Monday. Parking is easy — there's a free lot behind the building with the entrance on Elm St.

input: How late can I cancel without a fee?
context: Cancellation policy: free cancellation up to 24 hours before the appointment. Inside 24 hours, a $25 fee applies.
expected: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before your appointment. Inside that 24-hour window, a $25 fee applies.

input: Respond to an angry client: 'Your therapist was 20 minutes late!'
context: Incident: therapist ran 20 minutes late. Policy: apologize, offer to make it right with 15% off the next visit, do not blame staff by name.
expected: You're right to be frustrated — starting 20 minutes late isn't the experience we promise. I'd like to make it right with 15% off your next visit. Can I rebook you at a time that works better?

input: The client says the $140 massage is too expensive.
context: Service: 90-min deep tissue $140. Value points: licensed therapists, 90 full minutes hands-on, hot towels included. Policy: never discount on the spot; offer the 60-min $95 option instead.
expected: I understand — $140 is real money. What you're getting is 90 full minutes hands-on with a licensed therapist, hot towels included. If that stretches the budget, our 60-minute deep tissue at $95 is the same quality in a shorter session.

input: Do you sell gift cards?
context: Gift cards: available in any amount from $25 to $500. They never expire. Redeemable for services and products.
expected: Yes — gift cards are available in any amount from $25 to $500, they never expire, and they work for both services and products.
